Patrick Flynn's birthplace is disputed: the 1850 census (a_002) and 1860 census (a_009) both record Ireland, while the 1908 death certificate (a_012) records Pennsylvania. The 1850 census records Patrick, age 5, in the Thomas Flynn household in Schuylkill County, with birthplace listed as Ireland. The informant was an adult household member — most likely Thomas Flynn or his wife — who answered the enumerator's questions in person. The 1860 census records Patrick again in the same household ten years later, again with birthplace as Ireland, again from a household informant. These are original government documents made close in time to the events they describe, by informants with direct family knowledge. The 1908 death certificate, by contrast, records birthplace as Pennsylvania. The informant was James Brown, Patrick's son-in-law, who signed the certificate. Brown had no firsthand knowledge of where Patrick was born 63 years earlier; he was reporting what he understood or had been told about his father-in-law's origins.

The two census records are preferred. The household informants who provided the census information knew Patrick's birthplace from direct family knowledge — they raised him. James Brown, reporting in 1908, could not have known this fact firsthand. Two consistent records from proximate informants, taken close in time to the birth, outweigh one later record from a secondary informant with no firsthand access to the event. The most likely explanation for the error is a well-documented immigration-origin confusion pattern. Patrick was almost certainly born in Ireland and immigrated to Pennsylvania as a young child. By the time of his death, James Brown knew the family only as a Pennsylvania family. When asked where Patrick was born, Brown likely reported where Patrick grew up — Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania — rather than Ireland, either because he genuinely did not know Patrick had been born abroad or because he conflated ethnic origin with birthplace. A son-in-law who knew his father-in-law only in Pennsylvania, never having met him as a child, was in no position to know where Patrick had entered the world.
